right_defects.translation: by the vigilance of the Bishops

why: Right drops constantia in the sentence that crosses the break; left renders it.

left_defects.translation: which is not sufficient to overcome it

right_defects.translation: by the vigilance of the Bishops

why: Left renders the crossing sentence in full; right drops constantia at the break, and left's later slip is farther from the junction.
Both join Titum/Titum correctly without duplication; left turns the statement after the break into a question and interrupts the sentence with the running head.

right_defects.source: memoria cartarum ... revocatus a latentibus custodiis ... interceptus
right_defects.translation: because of the papers ... he was recalled by hidden guards and intercepted
who was spreading dangerous principles of faith in the year 1700

why: Right misattaches the hidden guards to the recall and misplaces the year 1700 in the first sentence after the break.

right_defects.source: Capituli Patronis hunc eligere ... Sic me Deus adjuvet
right_defects.translation: Capituli Patronis hunc eligere ... (left in Latin after the break)
rendered in English before the break and repeated in Latin after it

why: Right pulls the electors' oath across the break into page one and leaves the page-two text untranslated Latin; left splits it correctly.

left_defects.translation: from Quesnel's own mouth not only once
the old man lived on until December 2

right_defects.translation: the old man lived until December 2

why: Both handle the Alterum est / est catchword without duplication; each has one small omission of comparable weight and they share one.
